Climate zones 7A (39,168 kWh/unit/year), 6A (35,242 kWh), and 5A (33,805 kWh) exhibit the highest consumption due to long heating seasons and greater indoor- outdoor temperature differences. In contrast, warmer zones such as 1A (17,990 kWh), 2B (17,281 kWh), and 3B (14,978 kWh) have lower energy use, reflecting milder winters and minimal heating demand. Mixed and marine zones like 4C (20,065 kWh) and 3C (14,425 kWh) fall in between. Figure 16 shows that attic floor insulation upgrades result in the highest absolute energy savings in cold and mixed-humid climates. The greatest savings occur in zone zones 5A (738 kWh), followed by zones 5A (738 kWh), 3A (719 kWh), 4B (688 kWh/unit/year), and 6B (513 kWh). In contrast, warmer zones like 1A (125 kWh) and 2B (260 kWh) see lower savings due to smaller heating loads and more consistent baseline insulation. 21 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. Figure 16. Annual energy savings by climate zone for baseline compared to upgrade As shown in Figure 17, percent savings are highest in zones 3C (2.6%), 4B (3.0%), and 3A (3.4%). Despite high baseline consumption, zones 6A (1.6%) and 7A (1.5%) show relatively low percent savings, likely due to higher starting insulation levels, which reduce marginal gains. Similarly, hot climates such as 1A (1.0%) and 2B (1.5%) show limited savings due to minimal heating needs. These trends correspond with baseline attic insulation levels by climate zone (Figure 2). Zones like 1A, 3A, and 4B exhibit wide variability, including homes with low or no insulation (e.g., R-13, R-19, or uninsulated), creating greater upgrade potential. In contrast, zones 6B, 7A, and 8A tend to have higher, more uniform starting R-values, often R-30 or greater, leaving less room for improvement. Overall, attic insulation upgrades are most effective in climates with substantial heating demand and low baseline insulation. 23 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications.
